newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Bezeq tariff offer illegal.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Bezeq tariff offer illegal.

text.p: The opening of Israel's international calls market to competition was threatened with delay after Communications Minister Limor Livnat on Sunday accused Bezeq Israel Telecom of violating the law.

Livnat met with executives of Bezeq and its two prospective competitors on Sunday evening in a bid to reach an agreement that would allow the new, competitive market to begin on July 1 as scheduled, a communications ministry spokeswoman said.
But in the meantime the spokeswoman said Livnat had asked anti-trust authorities to intervene and to prosecute executives responsible for publicising the company's proposed international rates.

Livnat said Bezeq International, Bezeq's international phone service subsidiary, had violated Bezeq and anti-trust laws by advertising its proposed low tariffs last week before the ministry had approved them. The rates were as much as 80 percent below current tariffs, Bezeq said.

"Bezeq International took steps which in our opinion exploit its dominant position in the market and took these steps in order to frustrate the start of competition," Livnat said in a letter on Sunday to anti-trust commissioner David Tadmor.
Under the law Bezeq is subject to strict supervision during the first six months of the new competitive market, which the communications ministry spokeswoman said barred it from such actions.
Bezeq International said in a statement that the ministry knew in advance of the planned campaign and because the new tariffs were not yet in force the company had not violated the law.
"These numbers will only go into effect only when the government authorises them," a company spokeswoman told Reuters.

State-owned Bezeq launched the campaign last week in a mailing to customers in anticipation of competition from the two new providers -- Golden Lines, which is controlled by SBC Communications Inc, Italy's Stet and three Israeli partners, and Barak, controlled by Sprint Corp, France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom, Clal Israel and Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd.
Livnat defended her action, saying consumers would not benefit in the long run by what she called Bezeq's predatory prices.

"You might think, what is the problem with Bezeq International offering low prices?" Livnat told Israel Radio. "It's nice -- the consumers benefit. But that's not true because Bezeq is a monopoly. If it offers customers 'dumping prices' it won't allow international competitors to enter the competition."
A Communications Ministry spokeswoman said Livnat was only seeking to keep a level playing field. "We don't want to destroy Bezeq International," the spokeswoman said.
